pr_title: Fix ComputeEngineSSHHook to handle multiple parallel connections
pr_body:
This PR fixes https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/29258

The problem was caused by multiple processes updating metadata of the Compute Engine instance when running in parallel: methods _authorize_compute_engine_instance_metadata() and import_ssh_public_key() are used to upload metadata and import ssh keys. Both of them included making API requests to update information inside the instance. When making such requests in parallel all the processes were updating the same data simultaneously, that caused those problems listed in the issue.

The solution here is to use some kind of lock to prevent execution of critical part of the code by several processes at one time. As the Composer is a distributed system, all the processes are running separately, making connection between them hard.
As the solution in this case i have implemented a logic of creation separate GCS bucket that will hold a file that will be used as a lock for the processes: if the file exists and there is a string inside it - the lock is acquired. After the execution is finished, the lock will be released, so next process could take this lock next. The last process running will delete the bucket.

Note: when establishing connection using os_login, make sure that you have enabled such option for your instance in instance keys and that all of the connections you are trying to establish use the same value for the parameter: once you have enabled os_login for your instance, it will wait the exact type of keys to authenticate correctly. There is no option to mix different types of authentication for one instance.

> I am afraid this is going to introduce more problems than it solves.
> 
> There are few problems with it:
> 
> * you need ot be able to have service account that can create buckets - that's a new capability
> * bucket is deleted immediately when lock is released, which means that other tasks will have the bucket deleted while they are waiting for the lock. This will cause failures
> * this is very brittle and not self-healing. If you have one task abruptly killed while it holds the lock (happens when you have hardware failure for example) - your lock will remain and it will hold the whole DAG from re-running until you manually remove the lock
> * In the future when we have AIP-44 implemented, tasks won't be able to query the DB of Airflow directly so your query about parallel tasks will fail (when AIP-44 is complete we are going to forbid built-in operators in all providers to run any DB query).
> 
> So there are many things wrong here. I Cannot propose a different solution, but I think it should be based on the state of metadata - and metadata should be queried before they are updated. That might at least mitigate part of the problem. Ideally some kind of optiistic lock strategy on metadata would be great (i.e automatically updating version number that you can use to get optimisitc lock strategy - but I am afraid metadata API does not support it, maybe some other mechanism that provides a lock - but not based on manually managed GCS lock, something that will automatically release lock when the client gets killed. Not sure what it could be - but the solution proposed here is going IMHO to cause more problems than it solves.

Thank you for the ideas! Yes, looks like i was trying to solve the problem, but there are a lot of unpredictable problems that could happen during DAG execution. I will try to find something else here using the metadata you mentioned :)

Hi @potiuk !
Thank you for your ideas. I have rechecked the flow and changed the logic in the code:
now, when catching specific types of exceptions, the code will retry specified action once again until the maximum number of retries will be reached.
The decision about specific types of exceptions to be caught was made by investigating behavior of the connection in different cases:

- if os_login=False, then the instance metadata is used for authentication. In this case, when multiple parallel connections are trying to retrieve/change the metadata in API calls, the 412 error is thrown (either Airflow exception with 412 error message or HttpError(412) )

- if os_login=True, then the os_login is used for authentication. Multiple connections at the same time lead to SSHException trying to connect, the SSHException from paramiko library is thrown.

I have also modified method `_connect_to_instance()` to follow current logic. It was running infinitive loop until the connection was actually established. Now this logic is changed to use only 5 retries at a time. Then, if the connection is still not established, the process of generating and importing ssh public key will be repeated. It will ensure that no process is not stuck with the same public key trying to authenticate and failing.

@eladkal 
Could you check the changes when you have time? Thanks!

@kaxil @uranusjr 
Hi there! Could you also please take a look on the changes? Thanks :)
Way better approach with optimisitic update strategy and retries when it fails !

But when we start parallelism where multiple tasks are trying to connect to our GCE instance using ComputeEngineSSHHook at the same time,

@vasu2809 greetings!

Apache Airflow is a OSS project, so there are no specific people who could support or assist. Only people who bump into the same problem or know about a specific part of Airflow or specific provider.

This mostly refers to the issue with Google Provider and how it integrated with SSH Provider. Most possible that this hook doesn't propagate all settings to SSHOperator.

I would recommend investigating this first.
A lot of stuff in providers could be fixed locally, by creating your own hooks/operators and overwriting buggy parts or extending missing capabilities. That's basically how I did in the past. However a long term solution - contributes back to Airflow.

I don't feel confident with GCP and Google Provider, all I can do from my side is mark this issue as 'good first issue' and maybe someone could pick it up.
